candidate.title: Israel delays building contracts for E1 West Bank settlement after UK sanctions
candidate.excerpt: Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area. Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but…

publishedSummary: Israel has postponed issuing contracts for building a large West Bank settlement seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, The Guardian reports. The delay came days after the UK imposed sanctions on building firms operating in the area.
publishedSignificance: The E1 settlement is seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, and international sanctions are now a factor.
denial: Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street.
